question: How should the guru use the same procedure with the caruka and the tooth-stick?
premises: The same procedure is to be used again.
The guru should make the disciple take the caruka.
The tooth-stick is involved and its falling is read as before.
inference: By the same method, the guru has the disciple take the caruka and uses the falling of the tooth-stick as a sign in the same way as before.
uncertainties: Whether tatpātaḥ refers only to the tooth-stick or also echoes the earlier falling sign is slightly compressed in the verse.
plain_english: Using this very same procedure, the guru should have the disciple take the caruka and also the tooth-stick; its falling is to be understood just as before.
